purpose: Preregister a sixth independent FX8 mechanism batch before any Batch 6 Count, Return, win/loss, PF, p-value or Outcome is calculated or viewed.

EXP-P9-MTF-321.name: H1 Directional Path-Efficiency Continuation
EXP-P9-MTF-321.mechanism: A 24-observation H1 path with a large net displacement and little backtracking represents persistent order flow; continue in the net direction.

EXP-P9-MTF-322.name: H1 Same-Sign Run Exhaustion Reversal
EXP-P9-MTF-322.mechanism: The first completion of six consecutive same-sign H1 close changes with a large cumulative move marks short-horizon directional exhaustion; reverse once at the run boundary.

EXP-P9-MTF-323.name: Turn-of-Month Prior-Month Momentum
EXP-P9-MTF-323.mechanism: At 08:00 UTC on the first observed trading date of each month, continue the direction of the preceding 20 completed D1 closes when displacement is material relative to pre-decision D1 ATR.

EXP-P9-MTF-324.name: Friday Weekly Stretch Position-Squaring Reversal
EXP-P9-MTF-324.mechanism: At the fixed Friday 16:00 UTC H1 bar, a four-day displacement is reversed only when that bar retraces a fixed fraction of the stretch, representing weekly position reduction.

EXP-P9-MTF-321.independent_of_301_320: Uses net displacement divided by total absolute H1 path length. It does not use boundaries, EMA alignment, semivariance, calendar timing or cross-sectional ranks.

EXP-P9-MTF-322.independent_of_301_320: Uses the exact run length of return signs and triggers only at first run completion. No prior candidate defines an event from consecutive close-change signs.

EXP-P9-MTF-323.independent_of_301_320: Uses the first trading date of each month and prior 20 completed D1 momentum. Unlike 314 it is month-start continuation rather than last-date 16:00 reversal; unlike 315 it is not cross-sectional or Monday-only.

EXP-P9-MTF-324.independent_of_301_320: Uses a fixed Friday 16:00 weekly position-squaring reversal after a four-day displacement. It is not month-end fixing, weekend opening-gap reversion or a daily fixed-hour impulse.
